title: What are personal values and why do they matter?
citation: Sagiv, L., Roccas, S., & Oppenheim-Weller, S. (2015). Values and well-being. Positive psychology in practice: Promoting human flourishing in work, health, education, and everyday life, 103-120.
content:
What are personal values and why do they matter?

Personal values are the qualities and principles that matter most to you and guide the way you want to live. They are not about what you achieve, but about the kind of person you want to be in your relationships, work, health, and everyday life. Values act like a compass, helping you make choices that feel meaningful, even when life is difficult or uncertain.

Aren't values just goals I haven't achieved yet?

Values and goals are closely connected, but they are not the same thing. A goal is something you can complete, such as finishing a course or getting a promotion. A value is an ongoing direction, such as being curious, compassionate, or dependable. Even if a goal changes or is not achieved, you can still continue living according to your values every day.

Why do I feel unsettled when I act against my values?

Many people notice feelings of discomfort, frustration, or guilt when their actions do not match what is important to them. This happens because values provide a sense of direction and purpose. When there is a gap between how you want to live and how you are actually behaving, it can create an internal sense that something is not quite right. This discomfort is often a signal to reflect, rather than a sign that something is wrong with you.

What does living in line with my values actually look like?

Living according to your values does not mean feeling happy or motivated all the time. It means making choices that reflect what matters most, even when those choices are difficult. For example, someone who values kindness may choose to listen patiently during a disagreement, while someone who values health may go for a walk despite feeling unmotivated. Values are shown through consistent actions, not perfect behaviour.

Values vs goals: what's the difference?

Goals are destinations that can be reached and crossed off a list, while values are ongoing directions that continue throughout life. For example, graduating from university is a goal, but valuing learning can guide you long after graduation. Achieving a goal may bring satisfaction for a period of time, whereas living according to your values can provide a continuing sense of meaning and purpose.

Why do I feel lost even when nothing's obviously wrong?

This can happen when daily life becomes focused on routines, expectations, or achievements without enough attention to what genuinely matters personally. Reconnecting with your values can help explain why life feels unfulfilling and provide a clearer sense of direction, even if your external circumstances have not changed.

How do I identify and clarify my own values?

Values are discovered through reflection rather than found in a single moment. It can help to ask yourself what kind of person you want to be, what qualities you admire in others, or what you would like your relationships, work and daily life to stand for. Many people also find it helpful to explore their values with a therapist, particularly if they feel stuck or uncertain. Clarifying your values is about identifying what feels personally meaningful and using that as a guide for future choices.
